candidates.name: Josh Green
candidates.background: Governor since 2022 and an emergency room physician who kept working rural Big Island ERs while serving 14 years in the legislature. As lieutenant governor he was Hawaii's designated healthcare liaison leading the COVID-19 pandemic response, and he led homelessness policy statewide. Won the Aug 8, 2026 Democratic primary with about 82% seeking a second term.
priorities: Lower the cost of living and protect middle-class tax relief
Build housing and cut unsheltered homelessness (kauhale villages)
Healthcare access and rural health investment

cost.label: Doubled the earned income and food tax credits and pledges to 'protect the middle-class tax relief and credits families are already counting on' (Civil Beat Q&A)

health.label: ER physician; signed 22 healthcare bills in 2024 and exempted Medicare, Medicaid, and TRICARE medical services from the state excise tax (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Mixed: housing emergency proclamation to 'remove unnecessary regulations' and fast-track construction AND heavy state investment in affordable homes and kauhale villages that cut unsheltered homelessness 13% statewide (Civil Beat Q&A)

immigration.label: Local police 'should not be working on immigration work'; cooperate with DHS only over real criminal activity; 'we're a state that's built on immigration' (Hawaii Public Radio)

taxes.label: Mixed: signed 'the biggest tax cut for the middle class in Hawaii's history' while adding a new visitor climate fee raising about $100 million a year (Civil Beat Q&A)

climate.label: Enacted a first-of-its-kind climate impact fee on visitors, about $100 million a year 'walled off' for resilience projects (Civil Beat Q&A)

education.label: Signed HB 1890 raising teacher pay with annual step increases, plus school worker protections, community college aid, and cheaper school meals: 'we have to support the people who make those schools work' (Governor's office, July 13, 2026)

safety.label: Signed SB 3139, which 'expanded mental health crisis intervention' and strengthened the healthcare workforce, among 22 healthcare bills signed in June 2024 (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Signed the March 2023 law expanding abortion access and shielding Hawaii providers from out-of-state prosecution (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Signed SB 2239 (Act 67) on June 18, 2026, automatically registering eligible residents to vote at license renewal unless they opt out (Maui Now)

candidates.name: Gary Cordery
candidates.now: Owner, Kingdom Builders construction and real estate company
candidates.background: Construction and real estate business owner (Kingdom Builders, since 1998) and former church pastor who moved to Hawaii in 1982; describes himself as 'a husband, father and grandfather, businessman and community servant.' Finished third in the 2022 Republican primary for governor with 10.9%, then won the Aug 8, 2026 Republican primary with about 67%. Running mate is Daniel Anthony.
priorities: Cut the cost of living: no excise tax on food and medicine
Protect and expand Hawaii's income tax cuts

cost.label: Answer to cost of living is 'reducing taxes and fees': freeze property taxes for retirees, eliminate the general excise tax on food and medicine (Civil Beat Q&A)

housing.label: Mixed: 15,000 fee-simple homes at $400K-600K built on state lands AND 'amend the 5% of zoned land to 6%' so local families can buy in and build generational wealth (Civil Beat Q&A)

taxes.label: Protect and expand the recent income tax cuts; argues a $20.5 billion state budget for 1.4 million residents shows Hawaii overtaxes (Civil Beat Q&A)

climate.label: Questions whether the green fee is effective; wants hydrogen, fission, and small modular reactors explored alongside renewable goals (Civil Beat Q&A)

education.label: 'Offer a voucher program', get parents actively involved, and reduce union influence over school policy (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: Mixed: 'completely fund our police and investigative agencies' AND treat the meth epidemic and homelessness through individualized mental health and drug treatment (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Supports monitoring climate change but wants 'real, hard sciences' rather than 'politically driven research' (Ballotpedia survey)

immigration.label: Advocates fast processing with individual case evaluation and criticizes enforcement approaches of both administrations (Civil Beat Q&A)

climate.label: Opposes liquefied natural gas as a bridge fuel and favors solar panels on existing infrastructure (Civil Beat Q&A)

candidates.name: Jill Naomi Tokuda
candidates.now: U.S. Representative for Hawaii's 2nd District since 2023
candidates.background: Former state senator from Windward Oahu who has represented Hawaii's 2nd District in Congress since 2023. Renominated in the Aug 8, 2026 primary with 83 percent of the vote.

cost.label: Backs continued enhanced child tax credits, an expanded EITC, and 'increasing the minimum wage' (Tokuda campaign)

health.label: 'We have to reverse the $1.5 trillion in cuts to Medicaid and Medicare that will result in rural hospitals closing' (Civil Beat Q&A)

housing.label: Supports using 'federal resources to build, purchase, or preserve affordable housing' (Tokuda campaign)

immigration.label: Voted no on the Laken Riley Act's expanded immigration detention mandates (House Clerk roll 23, Jan 22, 2025)

climate.label: 'Hawaii is ideally situated to be a leader in renewable energy, harnessing resources like solar, wind, and hydropower' (Tokuda campaign)

education.label: 'Funding quality public education for students of all ages is one of the most valuable investments for the future of Hawaii' (Tokuda campaign)

repro.label: 'Reproductive decisions are deeply personal and should remain in the hands of women, not dictated by politicians' (Tokuda campaign)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act's documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement for voter registration (House Clerk roll 102, Apr 10, 2025)

nullNotes.taxes: campaign issues page and Civil Beat Q&A offer child tax credit and EITC expansions, targeted household credits that do not fit this axis per the calibration anchors; no position on raising or broadly cutting tax rates documented
nullNotes.safety: campaign issues page addresses only gun violence, which does not map to this axis; no policing or sentencing approach documented

candidates.name: Brenton Awa
candidates.background: Former TV news anchor from Ka'a'awa elected to the state Senate in 2022 and now its minority leader, one of three Republicans in the chamber. Says he would serve a single term and quit politics 'if we housed every Hawaiian.'

cost.label: Would 'increase the child tax credit to provide greater tax relief for families' and expand federal childcare assistance (Awa campaign)

health.label: Would 'expand federally funded community health centers across Hawaii that focus on care rather than copays' and require posted prices (Awa campaign)

housing.label: Would cap 'predatory investor buying' and expand down payment assistance so locals can afford homes (Awa campaign)

climate.label: Backs 'a balanced federal energy approach that maintains reliable, affordable power in Hawaii' (Awa campaign)

safety.label: Proposes 'temporary deployment of National Guard units to support local law enforcement in high crime areas' (Awa campaign)

democracy.label: 'If your numbers don't show up as the winner, you lost. Accept it'; says Joe Biden legitimately won 2020 (Civil Beat)

candidates.name: Edward Case
candidates.background: Centrist Democrat who has represented urban Honolulu's 1st District since 2019 after earlier House service in the 2000s. Renominated in the Aug 8, 2026 primary.

cost.label: Attacks the Jones Act and tariffs for adding 'thousands of dollars to each and every Hawaii family's costs every year'; his cost fix is reforming both, not price intervention (Civil Beat Q&A)

housing.label: Says the best federal housing tools are 'Jones Act and tariff reform, as each and both artificially jack up housing construction costs' (Civil Beat Q&A)

immigration.label: Mixed: supports legal immigration and opposes illegal immigration, but has 'strongly opposed how this administration is enforcing key parts of our laws'; voted no on the Laken Riley Act (Civil Beat Q&A; House Clerk roll 23)

climate.label: Would 'confront climate change deniers with scientific realities', backs Paris participation and renewable energy R&D funding (Civil Beat Q&A)

democracy.label: Voted yes on the SAVE Act's documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement for voter registration, one of a handful of Democrats to do so (House Clerk roll 102, Apr 10, 2025)

nullNotes.health: Civil Beat Q&A does not cover healthcare and his campaign materials were not located with a stated public-versus-private position
